title: Stalk of relative differentials is the differential module of the local rings
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $z\in X$, and put $s=f(z)$. Give $A=\mathcal O_{X,z}$ its $R=\mathcal O_{S,s}$-algebra structure through the stalk map of $f$. With the sheaf of relative differentials [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], module stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], and ring differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], there is a canonical $A$-linear isomorphism $$(\Omega^1_{X/S})_z\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega_{A/R}.$$ It sends the germ at $z$ of $\mathrm d_{X/S}a$, for a section $a$ of $\mathcal O_X$ on an open neighbourhood of $z$, to $\mathrm d_{A/R}(a_z)$. No finite-type, Noetherian, or smoothness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 08TE, lemma-stalk-module-differentials, applied to f^{-1} O_S -> O_X; scheme relative differentials are defined in morphisms.tex Tag 01UQ, definition-sheaf-differentials.

proof.text: Take the stalk of the additive universal sheaf derivation, using the preservation of filtered colimits by the forgetful functor from commutative rings to abelian groups. Its value on a germ a_z is (d a)_z. Represent two stalk elements on a common neighbourhood and apply the sheaf Leibniz rule and the germ scalar formula to prove Leibniz for this additive map. A base stalk element is a germ of a base section; the germ-stalk-map identity and d_app_app show that its image has differential zero. Thus obtain a derivation of O_X,z relative to O_S,f(z).

proof.text: For an O_X,z-module N and a derivation D of O_X,z relative to O_S,f(z), construct a sheaf derivation into the skyscraper module at z with coefficient N. On an open U it is the function sending a section a and a membership witness z in U to D(a_z). Additivity, Leibniz and restriction compatibility follow by the germ formulas. The value on f.app V b vanishes because its germ equals f.stalkMap z applied to b_f(z), on which D is zero. The source lemma derivationMk then makes it relative to the presheaf inverse image of O_S. No sheafification of that inverse image and no affine hypothesis is required.

proof.text: The stalk-skyscraper Hom equivalence is the existing proved source declaration Scheme.Modules.skyscraperHomEquiv in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.FlatPullbackStalk (the explicit scheme-module realization of the adjunction). Compose its inverse with relativeDifferentialsHomEquiv inverse, applied to the skyscraper derivation of step 2 for the universal ring derivation. This gives l:(Omega_X/S)_z -> Omega_(O_X,z/O_S,f(z)). The germ formula follows from Hom.stalkLinearMap_germ, skyscraperStalkEval_germ and relativeDifferentialsHomEquiv_symm_app_d. The same two injective Hom equivalences prove that two linear maps from the differential stalk are equal when they agree on differential germs.

proof.text: Apply ModuleCat.Derivation.desc to the derivation of step 1 to construct r:Omega_(O_X,z/O_S,f(z)) -> (Omega_X/S)_z. The composite r l agrees with the identity on every differential germ by the formulas of steps 1 and 3, hence is the identity by the extensionality just proved. To prove l r is the identity, use CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential.ext: every local ring element is a germ, and on its universal differential the same formulas and desc_d give equality. Consequently l is bijective, and LinearEquiv.ofBijective supplies the required linear equivalence.

proof.text: The equivalence has the required differential-germ formula by step 3. Any other equivalence with that formula has the same underlying linear map by the differential-germ extensionality from step 3; injectivity of LinearEquiv.toLinearMap gives equality. This proves existence and uniqueness without changing the theorem statement or imposing any additional hypotheses.
